ftm.office_official: Clerk of the Circuit Court, Probate Division
ftm.notes: Probate is done by appointment only. Applications can be submitted by email, mail, or in person. Original documents are required. The Clerk acts as a probate judge. Notice to Creditors opens the claim window and names the decedent + personal representative; probate rarely carries the property address (a separate assessor lookup fills it). Contact the personal representative / executor, never the deceased.

ftm.data_type: Foreclosure (first public signal for this state's process)
ftm.office_official: Clerk of the Circuit Court (Recorder of Deeds)
ftm.notes: Virginia is a nonjudicial / power-of-sale state. The first signal is a recorder-filed notice of default or a published trustee-sale notice, which hits the recorder index BEFORE the newspaper ad. Online access to recorded documents is by paid subscription only (VA Code § 17.1-277.6). Public notices, including foreclosure sales, may also be found in local newspapers like the Fredericksburg Free-Lance Star (fredericksburg.column.us).

ftm.data_type: Recorder / Register of Deeds - Lien & Deed Index
ftm.office_official: Clerk of the Circuit Court, Records & Recordation Services
ftm.notes: The Clerk is responsible for retaining all deeds and land records. Online access to recorded documents (including mechanic's, tax, HOA, child-support liens, and lis pendens) is by paid subscription only (VA Code § 17.1-277.6). Recording hours are Monday-Friday from 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM. A Virginia Land Record Cover Sheet is required for all documents to be recorded. GOTCHA: tax and child-support liens are indexed against the PERSON, not the parcel - name-match to the assessor roll.

Virginia is a tax deed state (usually no redemption after the sale). The Treasurer's office conducts auctions for land for sale due to unpaid real estate taxes. The list publishes as a legal notice weeks before the sale; market the owner before the auction. Information on upcoming sales is posted on the county website.

The Treasurer's office manages delinquent real estate taxes. While a specific 'pre-sale roll' portal isn't explicitly stated, the land sale information page is the primary source for tax-related property issues. Contact the Treasurer's office directly for the most current delinquent roll. Cities often levy their own property tax (a separate city delinquent list).

ftm.office_official: Department of Community Development, Code Enforcement Division
ftm.notes: The Code Enforcement Division investigates complaints regarding violations of the Spotsylvania County Code. Online access to specific violation records may require a public records request. Unincorporated county code offices are typically behind - records request only.

ftm.office_official: Department of Community Development, Code Enforcement Division
ftm.notes: Information regarding condemned or unsafe structures would fall under the purview of Code Enforcement. Specific lists of such properties are generally not available online and would likely require a public records request.

Eviction (unlawful detainer) cases are heard in the General District Court. To identify multiple-eviction landlords, one would need to pull the court's eviction docket and analyze the plaintiff (landlord) filings. This typically requires in-person research or a subscription to a legal data service, as online dockets may not be easily searchable by plaintiff across multiple cases. Hunt the PLAINTIFF (landlord), not the tenant; 2+ filings in 12 months = a tired landlord.

ftm_narrative: Data gaps to know about: SiftMap data (provider data) is low or zero in Spotsylvania County, VA for: Foreclosure notices, Tax sale list, Tax delinquent roll. These are proven deal-makers nationally, and nobody can buy them here, so the county pulls below are not a backup, they are the only way in: treat them as priority pulls. Also not in SiftMap here: Eviction filings, Code violations, Divorce filings.
Sources pulled straight from the county the day records publish, 30 to 90 days before paid data. 'Verify locally' means confirm the link before you work it.

read_me.Doors/deal: Live list size divided by the deals that list produced in the window. Lower is better: fewer doors to work per closed deal.
read_me.Lift: County baseline doors/deal divided by the signal's doors/deal. 3.0 means three times sharper than pulling the whole county.
read_me.Baseline: The whole county unfiltered, counted the same way; the denominator every signal is judged against.
read_me.Stack: Records sitting on two distress lists at once. Stacks are distress plus distress; AI is never AND-stacked on distress.
read_me.AI score: DataSift Investor AI likelihood-to-sell score, 0-100, a PARALLEL pull alongside the distress lists.
read_me.score-gated: Live AI-scored supply counts are provisioned per account, so a local doors/deal cannot be computed in this view. The deals and coverage are this county's own data.
read_me.Verify supply: The row tripped the verify rule (v2.1 coverage-aware: verify reasons annotate (churn: doors/deal < 5; small: list < 250) without demoting; only judicial notice lists and churn artifacts (doors/deal < 1) force P3. Volume floors: P1 needs >=2% of county deal flow or >=25 deals, P2 >=1% or >=12 deals): demand is real, treat the efficiency as directional until you price the live list.
read_me.Evidence A / B / C: from this county's own sold deals / cross-market benchmark / single-market anchor (Knox + Blount TN AI measurement)
read_me.Typical gross: Median of AVM value minus purchase price on clean deals: acquisition spread, not net profit.
read_me.Non-disclosure states: Sale prices are not public there, so deal-dollar columns are omitted; doors/deal and lift never use dollars.
